title: ENH: Add GAMESS-US FileIOCalculator
body:
[GAMESS-US](https://www.msg.chem.iastate.edu/gamess/) is a quantum chemistry program developed by the group of Mark Gordon at Iowa State University. It is a GTO code with many advanced quantum chemistry capabilities.

~~This is currently a minimal working prototype for basic HF calculations. I have not tested that this works for any other methods.~~

This calculator works with {R,U,RO}HF, DFT, MP2, and coupled cluster at least. It may fail to parse energies for other methods that I haven't tested.

Another thing: GAMESS-US is pretty annoying to run. It has a wrapper script named `rungms` written in `csh` (not even `tcsh`!) which does a lot of magic things, like moving files around and setting environment variables. This script must be edited for each cluster that it runs on, and customizing it is not at all easy.

One "helpful" feature of the `rungms` script is if it detects that you are running a calculation with the same name as a previously run calculation, it will fail with an error message stating you should back up your previous results. If you comment that part of `rungms` out, then the GAMESS-US executable will crash. You have to actually move/remove the previous results file (the "punchcard") in order to run a new calculation. I've locally modified my `rungms` script to do this, but we probably want the Calculator to take care of that for us. Of course, that requires knowing what `USERSCR` is set to in the `rungms` script, so....

TODO:
* [x]  Make the Calculator take care of this file moving problem described above
* [x]  Ensure compatibility with other non-RHF methods
* [x]  Write some tests
* [x]  Write documentation
author: ehermes

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
(Would gamess-us-out be more natural?)

The input and output have the same magic string, which means it's arbitrary whether we recognize a given file as one or the other.  It would be preferable to use different magic strings.  The format of output formats is normally detaile enough that we can recognize them reliably with a magic string (or pattern).
comments.label_reasoning: Input and output formats share the same magic string, making it ambiguous/arbitrary whether a file is recognized as input or output — a logic/design error in format identification.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Fantastically small class!

The set() method can (probably) be removed, setting instead the class attribute `discard_results_on_any_change = True` which the superclass will recognize as a common usecase for file io calculators.

I think we are looking to remove or try to remove several constructor keywords unless there are good arguments to keep them.  This is because constructing calculators in exotic ways is probably more suited for specialized factory methods.  This means maybe remove, unless you really use/believe in them, these: restart (unless explicitly tested, and preferably available as a separate function), ignore_bad_restart_file, and atoms.

About the atoms keyword see #475 .
comments.label_reasoning: The comment discusses class structure concerns: removing the set() method in favor of a class attribute, and removing unnecessary constructor keywords — all class design issues.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: About the file moving issue: You are probably in the best position to decide how to handle it.  I would consider asking python to create a tempdir for each calculation, then remembering the tempdir within `self.results` in order to retrieve results.
comments.label_reasoning: Suggestion to use a tempdir per calculation and store it in results — a structural improvement to how calculations and their results are organized.

comments.author: ehermes
comments.body:
The problem is that these files are generally *not in the working directory*. The relevant files are stored in `$USERSCR`, which is a directory set by the user in `rungms`. It's commonly set to a scratch directory, like `/scratch/$USER`, but this is definitely not guaranteed to be the location.

So let's assume that the user has GAMESS-US set up the way the like it with a customized `rungms` script, and now they want to be able to use GAMESS-US from ASE. How do we make sure that ASE knows where $USERSCR is? There are many different ways we could go about this, but I'm not yet sure what the path of least resistance is.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I'm probably not providing too much value since I don't know much about how rungms works, but

1) user needs to tell ASE `$USERSCR` (simple but annoying).
2) ASE generates rungms.  Probably not an option in general, but we could generate a sample rungms which we know will work.

I assume it's next to impossible to extract `$USERSCR` without also running the calculation (getting more than we bargained for).

comments.author: ehermes
comments.body:
>ASE generates rungms.

Definitely not feasible. There's too much going on in that file...

>I assume it's next to impossible to extract `$USERSCR` without also running the calculation (getting more than we bargained for).

That gave me an idea, actually. I don't think we want to try to parse a `csh` script, but we actually *can* run the script with a bogus input name. The version of `rungms` that ships with the source code will print USERSCR, along with other information. So we can try to run `rungms` with a non-existent input file name, ignore the failure, and parse USERSCR. If that fails, we can require the user to provide USERSCR manually.

I just pushed a commit which (as promised) adds complexity to the GAMESSUS calculator with just this functionality.

comments.author: askhl

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: maybe round instead of truncate?
comments.label_reasoning: Truncating instead of rounding is a logic error that can produce incorrect numerical results.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: perhaps use `check_call(command, shell=True)` since that will fail loudly rather than silently.  Otherwise it'll go on to read `<prefix_test>.log` which would presumably fail anyway (but the reason would be less obvious).
comments.label_reasoning: Using `call` instead of `check_call` ignores the subprocess return code, silently swallowing failures instead of raising an error.

comments.author: ehermes
comments.body: The `get_userscr` function tries to figure out the USERSCR environment variable that is defined in the `rungms` script. It does this by executing `rungms` on a non-existent input file, which causes the `rungms` command to print its header and exit with an error. We fully expect this command to fail (in fact, if it *doesn't* fail, that's a problem).

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Ah of course.  But some kind of error handling would be appropriate since it might fail to fail correctly, and this could be all the more tricky to figure out for someone working with it.  (A comment would be appropriate also)

comments.author: ehermes
comments.body: I think I made it a bit more robust. The function uses `call` now instead of `Popen` (or `check_call`), and it opens the potentially non-existent log file in the idiomatic Python way. I tried to suppress any exceptions that would be raised by the execution of `command` or parsing of the log file, since a failure here is not necessarily fatal, and I suspect will be somewhat common.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using check_call with shell=True to fail loudly on errors.
